title: More Than 500 Volunteers to Clean Up Zacate Creek as TAMIU Marks 17th Make a Difference Day
excerpt: Student volunteers from Texas A&M International University and Laredo College will team up Saturday, Oct. 24, for the 17th annual Make a Difference Day, cleaning and beautifying four sites along Zacate Creek.
content:
Laredo’s college students are rolling up their sleeves for their city again. More than 500 student volunteers from Texas A&M International University (TAMIU) and Laredo College will fan out along Zacate Creek on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, for the 17th annual Make a Difference Day, according to TAMIU.

The National Day of Service runs from 9 a.m. to noon and will focus on four sites along the creek. Students, faculty and staff will pick up trash, cover graffiti and take on beautification projects aimed at caring for the local environment and strengthening community connections, the university said.

“Through this collaborative effort, we hope to make a lasting, positive impact on our community while encouraging students to take an active role in environmental stewardship and the care of our shared public spaces,” said Priscilla A. Cadena, program manager in TAMIU’s Office of Student Affairs, according to the university.

The event is led by the Office of Student Affairs together with the Student Government Association’s Leaders Organizing Volunteer Events (L.O.V.E.) Committee, with support from community partners including the City of Laredo, Laredo College, the LISD Transportation Department, Nature Fresh Farms, Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages, the Rio Grande International Study Center and H-E-B, according to TAMIU.

Since 2010, university volunteers have completed community-wide projects benefiting organizations such as Habitat for Humanity, Volunteers Serving the Need, the Laredo Animal Care Facility and the Ruthe B. Cowl Rehabilitation Center, the university said. Seventeen years in, Make a Difference Day remains one of the clearest examples of Laredo’s students showing up for Laredo.
